display.title: Havdalah: Why We Smell Besamim When Shabbos Ends
display.summary_short: A short Mitzvah Time review: at Havdalah we smell fragrant spices to cheer us up when the extra Shabbos neshamah returns to Hashem.
display.summary_long: A short Mitzvah Time lesson from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, part of a series on the laws of Havdalah, the prayer said as Shabbos ends. Uncle Yossi reviews why we use besamim, fragrant spices, and say the brachah Borei Minei Besamim. Every Shabbos Hashem gives each Jew a special gift to keep for the whole day: the neshamah yeseirah, an extra holy soul that makes us feel so holy and so happy. When Shabbos is over we must return this heavenly gift to Hashem, and we are sad to say goodbye. So we smell the besamim to cheer us up and to encourage us to wait patiently until next Friday evening, when the extra neshamah will come back once again. In the full program, a phone quiz on these laws follows.
display.lesson: The besamim at Havdalah cheer us as the extra Shabbos neshamah leaves, until it returns next Shabbos.
